narrative.intro: AMI Metals has $1.5B in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date, across 9 awards with an average award size of $164M. Obligations rose significantly year over year, up 3016758.9% versus the prior comparable period. The Department of Homeland Security accounted for the vast majority of FY2026 obligations, providing $1.5B. The Department of Defense is a much smaller buyer in the current year, with $13.5K in obligations. Process, Physical Distribution, and Logistics Consulting Services is the primary NAICS market for AMI Metals in FY2026 to date at $1.5B, while Other Support Activities for Air Transportation shows $13.5K. Historical yearly obligations show minimal activity before FY2026, with FY21 at $9.8K, FY22 at $165K, FY23 at $109K, FY24 at $346K, and FY25 at $48.9K. Current-year totals are partial and represent fiscal year to date activity, not full fiscal year results.

sections.heading: What changed for AMI Metals in FY2026 to date?
sections.body: Obligations jumped to $1.5B in FY2026 to date, up 3016758.9% year over year. The Department of Homeland Security provided $1.5B of those obligations. Prior fiscal years show much smaller obligations, with FY25 at $48.9K and FY24 at $346K. The concentration in one year and one agency explains the sharp year-over-year change.

sections.heading: Who are AMI Metals' main federal customers and markets?
sections.body: The Department of Homeland Security is the main customer with $1.5B in obligations in FY2026 to date. The Department of Defense appears with $13.5K in obligations in the same period.
